subject: Log export delivery & retention options — post-call recap
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap — log export delivery & retention options

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for taking the time today — helpful to hear Olive Health's compliance priorities. Quick recap and the asks you requested during the call so we have a shared plan: 

1) What you asked for from Redwood:
  - A sample export of "who/what/when" access logs (fields & example rows).
  - Delivery options: S3 push, secure SFTP, or daily email CSV (syslog also optional).
  - Retention and tiering guidance (default 30d, options to extend to 180d / 365d).
  - Guidance on PII redaction at export-time vs. including identifiers for audit.

2) Our proposed immediate next steps:
  - We will share a sample export schema and an example CSV (attached).
  - Follow-up technical note on redaction options and how they affect indexing/search.
  - Quote for retention >30 days and any SLA language around log availability.

Attached: redwood_log_export_schema_v1.csv (schema + sample rows).

Action items for you: please confirm which delivery mechanism you prefer (S3 / SFTP / syslog) and the minimum fields you need in the exported rows. That will let us produce a short mapping doc and the pricing delta for retention beyond 30 days.

I can also book a quick 30-minute follow-up if you want to run through the mapping live: https://cal.com/redwood/tessa-30

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
mobile: +1 (415) 555-0198

[Attachment: redwood_log_export_schema_v1.csv]

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Olive Health Security Team <security@olivehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — log export delivery & retention options

Thanks Tessa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Delivery: preferred is S3 push (pre-signed put or cross-account role). SFTP acceptable as fallback. Syslog less ideal because we want immutable object storage for audits.
- Retention: baseline 30 days is fine for operational needs; compliance wants the option for 180 days for specific user buckets (e.g., escalations / investigations). For now, can you show a tiered pricing example?
- Fields: required fields are user_id (internal id), resource_path, action (read/write/delete), timestamp (ISO8601), actor_ip, request_id, and any request payload hash. We prefer not to include raw PII (names, emails) in the export.
- Redaction: we need an explanation of redaction-at-export vs. redaction-in-storage — if Redwood can redact identifiers before export, that is preferred. If not, we need a mitigation plan for secure delivery and encrypted-at-rest exports.

Also can you confirm the format options (CSV vs JSON lines) and whether you support column encryption or tokenization for specific fields in flight?

Samir Khan
Head of InfoSec | Olive Health
samir.khan@olivehealth.com
+1 (617) 555-0134

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@olivehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 Dec 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — log export delivery & retention options

Samir — appreciate the specifics, very helpful. Short answers up front, with attached mapping for your review: 

- Delivery: we support S3 push via cross-account role (recommended) and pre-signed URLs for customers who prefer not to share roles. SFTP delivery is also available but we consider S3 the most reliable for immutable audit storage.
- Formats: both newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) and compressed CSV (gzip) are available. NDJSON preserves nested fields (useful for request metadata).
- Redaction: Redwood can perform export-time redaction rules (we can redact or hash specified fields). Redaction is configurable per-export; we will include a sample mapping in the attachment that shows hashed_email and hashed_user_id examples. Note: redaction at export means the original identifiers are not present in the export; it does not remove them from the primary platform logs used for live debugging unless you explicitly request end-to-end redaction.
- Column encryption/tokenization: we support field-level encryption for exports using customer-managed keys (KMS). We can provide envelope encryption to S3 with a customer KMS key.

Attached: export_mapping_v1.csv — this maps our canonical fields to the columns you asked for and shows an example of hashed vs raw values.

Next steps I propose:
  1) You confirm delivery choice (S3 preferred) and whether you need KMS-protected exports.
  2) Confirm which fields must be redacted vs retained hashed.
  3) We will produce a short pricing addendum for retention tiers (30 / 180 / 365 days) and an SLA blurb for log delivery (S3 delivery SLA 99.9% for daily pushes).

If that looks right I'll schedule a 30-min technical follow-up and include an engineer to do a hands-on walk-through.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: export_mapping_v1.csv]

Looping in on pricing and SLA ask — thanks for drafting the mapping, Tessa. Two quick items we want to capture before the next call: 

1) Pricing impact: we need to prepare a short appendix that shows monthly incremental cost for 180d and 365d retention by log volume band (small / medium / large). Can you confirm the expected daily ingestion volume range we should model? Samir, if you can provide an approximate daily indexed event count (or avg bytes/day) that will let us size and price.

2) SLA language: Laura, can you provide a 1-2 line blurb for the contract that covers export delivery window and availability (example: "Redwood will push daily export files to the customer's designated S3 bucket within a 24-hour window; target delivery SLA 99.9% per calendar month").

Samir — if you can send the volume estimate I will turn around an appendix and we can discuss on the proposed technical follow-up.

Thanks,
